title: Private orchestrator reconnect surge during version rollouts — DNS resolution backoff & connection regeneration regression
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a staged rollout of private orchestrator v3.7.1 to several VPC clusters, we observed a coordinated reconnect surge from agent nodes to control plane endpoints that overwhelmed ephemeral connection quotas and caused intermittent control plane auth timeouts and DNS resolution latencies. Multiple customers experienced degraded API responsiveness and failed rolling upgrades in affected regions.
timeline: 2026-03-01 02:10 UTC — Canary cluster upgrade started (10% of target fleet).
2026-03-01 02:17 UTC — Monitoring alerted: control plane TCP connection queue climbed above expected baseline for the canary region.
2026-03-01 02:22 UTC — DNS cache churn observed on control plane hosts; average resolution latency increased from 8ms to 240ms.
2026-03-01 02:28 UTC — Canary rollout halted; automatic rollback triggered but many agents had already reconnected and triggered duplicate session establishment attempts.
2026-03-01 02:45 UTC — Incident declared; mitigation runbook executed to stagger reconnect windows and increase DNS cache TTL for control plane records.
2026-03-01 06:15 UTC — Normalized traffic after rolling back to previous orchestrator version and applying temporary DNS/connection fixes.
impact: Affected three enterprise private VPC clusters across two regions. Observed 10–25% higher request latencies for management plane APIs and several failed upgrade attempts requiring manual intervention. Revenue-impacting customer SLAs were degraded for ~4 hours for impacted tenants.
root_cause: A change in the orchestrator agent reconnection logic (throttled exponential backoff shortened to ensure faster recovery) interacted poorly with a simultaneous change that aggressively cleared local DNS caches on upgrade. The combination caused large groups of agents to attempt reconnection within a narrow window, exceeding ephemeral port and connection multiplexing limits on control plane frontends. Control plane side DNS resolver configuration did not prioritize negative caching or resolve timeouts, amplifying resolution latency under load.
contributing_factors: No deterministic preflight check to detect reduced backoff windows before rollout.
DNS TTL and local cache invalidation were coupled with agent restart sequence, causing synchronized stale-resolution refreshes.
Control plane connection queuing thresholds were conservative and did not expose graceful degradation (no soft-fail path to reject non-critical agent reconnections).
Insufficient telemetry on per-agent reconnect storm behavior; dashboards aggregated across clusters and masked per-region spikes.
mitigations_taken: Immediate: Abort rollout and roll back agents to v3.7.0 in affected clusters.
Immediate: Increased DNS cache TTL for control plane service records from 5s to 60s for the affected rollout window.
Immediate: Applied temporary rate-limiter on new agent session creations at control plane frontends to smooth bursts.
Short-term: Deployed a hotfix that reintroduces a randomized backoff jitter and a minimum backoff floor for agent reconnect attempts.
action_items: AI-1: Add a preflight validation job in the rollout pipeline to detect agent backoff parameter regressions by simulating reconnect patterns. Owner: Marco Sánchez. Due: 2026-03-18.
AI-2: Implement per-region reconnect telemetry and a reconnect storm alert (SLO breach when >X reconnects/min per region). Owner: Priya Rao. Due: 2026-03-22.
AI-3: Decouple DNS cache invalidation from agent restart lifecycle; introduce staged cache flush with randomized jitter. Owner: Linh Tran. Due: 2026-03-28.
AI-4: Increase ephemeral socket and connection queue monitoring with automated auto-scaling knobs for control plane frontends. Owner: Devops team (lead: Omar Haddad). Due: 2026-04-05.
AI-5: Update rollout runbook to include mandatory canary soak metrics for DNS latency and connection queue depth before proceeding past canary. Owner: SRE Docs working group. Due: 2026-03-15.
AI-6: Create a regression test in CI that runs a small-scale reconnect storm against a control-plane emulator to validate backoff policies. Owner: QA automation (lead: Mei Chen). Due: 2026-03-30.

AI-7: Postmortem review with Product and Security to evaluate whether connection throttling could be misinterpreted as an availability issue and to review customer communication templates. Owner: Aisha Patel. Due: 2026-03-12.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight job is green and prevents pipeline promotion when agent backoff/jitter fall outside approved ranges.
Reconnect storm alert fires in the test environment and notifies SRE on-call at <oncall>/pagerduty.
DNS cache invalidation is staggered in rollout staging and verified with synthetic checks that ensure no synchronous re-resolve spike.
Control plane frontends demonstrate autoscaling responding to a synthetic reconnect spike in performance lab.

2026-03-09 — Design feedback: suggest a Control Plane health widget in Console to display live connection queue depth per region (linked as a product ticket).

retrospective: We underestimated interactions between two unrelated changes (DNS cache invalidation behavior and backoff policy). Ship small behavioral changes separately when possible.
Lack of per-region telemetry masked the severity until customers reported issues — invest in higher fidelity observability for control plane metrics.
Runbooks must include explicit safety gates for infrastructure signals (DNS latency, connection queue depth) before promoting rollouts.
